mdk-001.back: Puddle ducks, divers, mergansers, sea ducks (85%).

mdk-020.front: By when are about 90% of mallard drakes back in colour?
mdk-020.back: Mid November, in a California study (75%).

mdk-021.front: How do you tell a young duck in the hand?
mdk-021.back: Notched tips on tail feathers (75%). In mallards the notch is unreliable from early September (70%).

mdk-025.front: Slate grey, white chicken bill. Legal?
mdk-025.back: American coot: legal, its own limit of 10 a day (99%).

mdk-026.front: Thin red bill with teeth. Duck or not?
mdk-026.back: Merganser: a duck, counts in your 8 (95%).

mdk-027.front: Daily duck limit and the four restricted species?
mdk-027.back: 8 a day. Inside it: 4 pintail, 4 canvasback, 2 goldeneye (both kinds), 2 harlequin (99%).

mdk-042.front: Do ducks have a true crop?
mdk-042.back: No. The gullet stretches to store food (80%).

mdk-043.front: How much grain can a mallard hold in its gullet?
mdk-043.back: Up to about 113 g, a quarter pound (75%).

mdk-044.front: Why do diving ducks have bigger gizzards?
mdk-044.back: They eat hard food like clams and snails (75%).
